chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding
a man who dies while his wife is under him (married to him) and he is absent. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should observe the waiting period from the day his death reaches her.'
ai.seo_question: When does a widow's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the commencement of the widow's waiting period (iddah) when the husband dies in absence, establishing that the timeline begins upon the receipt of news rather than the actual date of death. This ruling ensures legal certainty for the woman, allowing her to manage her affairs and remarry once the four months and ten days are completed from the moment she is informed, a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding
the man who dies and under him (married to him) is a woman, and he is absent. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She should observe the waiting period from the day (the news) of his death reaches her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “About the case of a man who dies and leaves behind a widow and he is absent, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘She must commence her ‘Iddah (waiting period) from the day she receives the news of his death.’”
